texts: About 30 percent of heart transplant recipients have cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) at 5 years: C.
In the picture, five years on, three of ten transplanted hotels have crowns whose spikes are evenly narrowed by white scale.

CAV is an immune-driven, diffuse and concentric thickening of the intima along the whole length of the coronary arteries, unlike the focal plaques of ordinary atherosclerosis, so it is rarely suited to bypass or stenting.
It rises to about half of recipients by 10 years and is a leading cause of late death and retransplantation.
Memory hook: three crowns in ten furred with white scale after five years.
